The '''2012–13 Ligue 1''' was the 75th season since its establishment.<ref>{{cite news|title=Palmarès: Les champions de France depuis 1932/1933 |url=http://new.lfp.fr/ligue1/palmares |work=[[Ligue de Football Professionnel]] |access-date=23 April 2011 |language=fr |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110419073300/http://new.lfp.fr/ligue1/palmares |archive-date=19 April 2011 }}</ref> [[Montpellier HSC|Montpellier]] were the [[2011–12 Ligue 1|defending champions]]. The league schedule was announced in April 2012 and the fixtures were determined on 30 May.<ref name="80_ans">{{cite news |title=Présentation de la saison de Ligue 1 |url=http://www.lfp.fr/ligue1/article/presentation-de-la-saison-de-ligue-1.htm |work=[[Ligue de Football Professionnel]] |date=30 May 2012 |access-date=30 May 2012 |language=fr |archive-date=31 May 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120531224456/http://www.lfp.fr/ligue1/article/presentation-de-la-saison-de-ligue-1.htm |url-status=dead }}</ref> The season began on 10 August and ended on 26 May 2013.<ref>{{cite news |title=Le calendrier général 2012/2013 adopté |url=http://www.lfp.fr/uploads/fichiers/CALENDRIER_GENERAL_SAISON_2012_2013.pdf?org=tinymce |work=Ligue de Football Professionnel |access-date=5 April 2012 |language=fr |archive-date=17 April 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120417015935/http://www.lfp.fr/uploads/fichiers/CALENDRIER_GENERAL_SAISON_2012_2013.pdf?org=tinymce |url-status=dead }}</ref> A winter break was in effect from 24 December to 12 January 2013.<ref>{{cite news |title=Le calendrier général 2012/2013 adopté |url=http://www.lfp.fr/corporate/article/le-calendrier-general-2012-2013-adopte.htm |work=Ligue de Football Professionnel |date=5 April 2012 |access-date=5 April 2012 |language=fr |archive-date=2 April 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190402191319/https://www.lfp.fr/corporate/article/le-calendrier-general-2012-2013-adopte.htm |url-status=dead }}</ref>

The season marked the 80th anniversary of professional football in France.<ref name="80_ans"/> In addition, German [[Sportswear (activewear)|sportswear]] company [[Adidas]] became the official provider of match balls for the season after agreeing to a long-term partnership with the [[Ligue de Football Professionnel]].<ref name="80_ans"/><ref>{{cite news |title=Puma délogé par Adidas et Uhlsport |url=http://www.sport.fr/football/ligue-1-puma-deloge-par-adidas-et-uhlsport-221916.shtm |work=Sport.fr |date=10 June 2011 |access-date=30 May 2012 |language=fr |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140408214712/http://www.sport.fr/football/ligue-1-puma-deloge-par-adidas-et-uhlsport-221916.shtm |archive-date=8 April 2014 |url-status=dead  }}</ref> To commemorate the 80th anniversary, adidas unveiled an exclusive ball, known as ''Le 80'', for the new season.

Since France dropped from fifth to sixth place in the [[UEFA coefficient#League coefficient|UEFA association coefficient rankings]] at the end of the 2011–12 season, the league's third place team, [[Olympique Lyonnais|Lyon]] qualified for the [[2013–14 UEFA Champions League#Third qualifying round|third qualifying round]] of the [[2013–14 UEFA Champions League]], having previously been placed in the playoff round.<ref>{{cite news |title=UEFA: La France perd sa 5e place |url=http://fr.sports.yahoo.com/04042012/79/uefa-la-france-perd-sa-5e-place.html |work=[[Yahoo!]] |date=4 April 2012 |access-date=22 April 2012 |language=fr |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120407123553/http://fr.sports.yahoo.com/04042012/79/uefa-la-france-perd-sa-5e-place.html |archive-date=7 April 2012 |url-status=dead  }}</ref>

On 12 May, [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]] won the league title after a 1–0 away win against Lyon.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/22506180|title= David Beckham's Paris St-Germain clinch French title|date=12 May 2013|work=BBC Sport|access-date=14 May 2013 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://espnfc.com/uk/en/report/342602/report.html?soccernet=true&cc=5739 |title= PSG wrap up title|date=12 May 2013|work=ESPN|access-date=14 May 2013 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url= http://espnfc.com/blog/_/name/parissaint-germain/id/1073?cc=5739|title=PSG's 19-year wait for a third title is over|date=12 May 2013|work=ESPN|access-date=14 May 2013 }}</ref>

== Teams ==
There were three promoted teams from [[Ligue 2]], replacing the three teams that were relegated from Ligue 1 following the [[2011–12 Ligue 1|2011–12 season]]. A total of 20 teams competed in the league with three clubs suffering relegation to the second division, Ligue 2. All clubs that secured Ligue 1 status for the season were subject to approval by the [[Direction Nationale du Contrôle de Gestion|DNCG]] before becoming eligible to participate.<ref name = dncg_rulings>The DNCG is responsible for overseeing the legal and financial accounts of professional football clubs in France. If clubs operating in [[French football]] didn't meet the DNCG's expectations, they would face sanctions, such as relegation.</ref>

Bastia became the first club to achieve promotion to Ligue 1. The club clinched the second division title on 1 May 2012 with three matches to spare after defeating [[FC Metz|Metz]] 3–0 at the [[Stade Armand Cesari]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Le SC Bastia champion! |url=http://www.lfp.fr/ligue2/article/le-sc-bastia-champion.htm |work=[[Ligue de Football Professionnel]] |date=1 May 2012 |access-date=1 May 2012 |language=fr |archive-date=9 July 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180709100021/https://www.lfp.fr/ligue2/article/le-sc-bastia-champion.htm |url-status=dead }}</ref> Bastia is making its return to the first division after a seven-year absence and is entering Ligue 1 on a run of two consecutive promotions.<ref>{{cite news |title=Bastia, sept ans de réflexion... |url=http://www.unfp.org/a-la-une/article/bastia-sept-ans-de-reflexion-02052012-6450.html |work=[[National Union of Professional Footballers]] |date=2 May 2012 |access-date=2 May 2012 |language=fr |archive-url=https://archive.today/20121228082248/http://www.unfp.org/a-la-une/article/bastia-sept-ans-de-reflexion-02052012-6450.html |archive-date=28 December 2012 |url-status=dead  }}</ref> The club had earned promotion to Ligue 2 after winning the [[2010–11 Championnat National|2010–11 edition]] of the [[Championnat National]].

[[Stade de Reims|Reims]] and [[Troyes AC|Troyes]] became the second and third clubs, respectively, to earn promotion to Ligue 1 alongside the champions Bastia.<ref>{{cite news |title=Football: Troyes et Reims promus en Ligue 1 |url=http://www.20minutes.fr/ledirect/932999/football-troyes-reims-promus-ligue-1 |work=20 Minutes |date=11 May 2012 |access-date=11 May 2012 |language = fr}}</ref> Both clubs achieved promotion with one game to spare following league victories on 11 May 2012, which positioned each club in second and third place permanently. Reims, which is a six-time Ligue 1 champion, is returning to the first division after over 33 years playing in the lower divisions.<ref>{{cite news |title=Football: Reims et Troyes promus en Ligue 1 |url=http://www.lemonde.fr/sport/article/2012/05/11/football-reims-et-troyes-promus-en-ligue-1_1700261_3242.html |work=[[Le Monde]] |date=11 May 2012 |access-date=11 May 2012 |language = fr}}</ref> During those 33 years, the club underwent [[liquidation]] and had all aspects of the club (its records, trophies, etc.) auctioned off. Troyes is returning to Ligue 1 after spending four years playing in Ligue 2. During its five-year spell outside the first division, Troyes also played in the [[Championnat National]], the third level of French football.<ref>{{cite news |title=Troyes une montée en Ligue 1 qui a surpris tout le monde |url=http://actu.voila.fr/actualites/documents/2012/05/11/troyes-une-montee-en-ligue-1-qui-a-surpris-tout-le-monde_2874298.html |work=Voila |date=11 May 2012 |access-date=11 May 2012 |language=fr }}{{Dead link|date=June 2023 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

=== Scoring ===
* First goal of the season: [[Souleymane Camara]] for Montpellier against Toulouse (<small>''10 August 2012''</small>)
* Fastest goal of the season: '''27 seconds''' – [[Zlatan Ibrahimović]] for Paris Saint-Germain against Lille (<small>''2 September 2012''</small>)
* Latest goal of the season: '''90+5 minutes''' – [[Ilan (footballer)|Ilan]] for Bastia against Reims (<small>''18 August 2012''</small>)
* Largest winning margin: '''5 goals'''
** Valenciennes 6–1 Lorient (<small>''20 October 2012''</small>)
** Nice 5–0 Valenciennes (<small>''13 January 2013''</small>)
** Lille 5–0 Lorient (<small>''7 April 2013''</small>)
* Highest scoring game: '''8 goals'''
** Lorient 4–4 Ajaccio (<small>''28 October 2012''</small>)
* Most goals scored in a match by a single team: '''6 goals'''
** Valenciennes 6–1 Lorient (<small>''20 October 2012''</small>)
* Most goals scored in a match by a losing team: '''3 goals'''
** Valenciennes 3–4 Bastia (<small>''30 March 2013''</small>)
** Toulouse 3–4 Nice (<small>''6 April 2013''</small>)
